I have a degree in English education, and I love to help people advertise their goods and services. Perhaps someone will buy their goods from me, and I will make money too. I would love to work in advertising, but to start with, I would like to work with brands as a social media manager, content creator, or generator. I don't know so much about advertising on digital media or social media management. Still, I want to start a business to help people and generate income to pay bills in the next 20days. I want to take advantage of every free AI tool, although I currently have access to CapCut Pro and love to tell stories. How should I go about this? I need a step-by-step, workable, and realistic strategic plan.  In addition, I have a flair for giving people advice about job seeking and the reality of choosing or settling for a 9-to-5 in Nigeria. I also share my experiences as a 9-to-5 who switched to content creation or built a brand in advertising.  

What are the key things here, and how can I organise all this and start from where I am? I don't have a laptop. All I have now is a mobile device. I have worked in a consulting firm, an eye clinic, a telecom company, taught in a school, as a Personal assistant to an executive secretary,  and as a real estate telesale marketer. I will like to help pptential employees know what it feels like on such jobs as well as give feedback to hiring managers and employers but not necessarily to the last two groups as i hope to get returns from my knowledge shared from job seekers and cv rewriting gigs or build a community that looks out for one another with an end goal of having a community that has skills that are appreciated and seen and helped to connect them to potential recruiters. 

I want you to read and organise all this in a structured way and work with me, suggesting the best platforms to launch on, what to do, and the statistics of success rate if I do it the way suggested. I have a WhatsApp business page but haven't registered my business name successfully, although I am on it. I do not have all the funds to register as a company yet.

You're a German UX researcher. Create me a table of the following questions. One column with the original questions, the second for German translations in Du/Dich/Deine informal language, and the third in Sie formal:

Understanding the Status Quo
To start, could you please walk me through your typical process, from the moment you post a new job on a platform like ours to the moment you decide which handful of candidates you want to interview? What are your biggest challenges with your current approach?

What ATS do they use?

What jobs do they hire for?

How many applications do they get?

Tell me about a time you managed a job opening that received a surprisingly high number of applications. How did that volume impact your day-to-day workflow and your ability to screen effectively?

Thinking about that same role, can you describe what separated the candidates you immediately dismissed from those you paused to consider more deeply? What specific signals were you looking for?

Do you (in any circumstances) look at candidates who do not meet your most basic requirements? 

When you review a candidate's profile or application, what information helps you feel confident that you can 'sell' this person to the hiring manager? What makes a profile feel compelling?

When you think about the candidate pools you get from different sources, like HeyJobs, Stepstone, Indeed, LinkedIn, or others, what differences, if any, stand out to you in how the candidates are presented?

"Gold Candidate" Experience
When you see that 'Gold Candidate' tag next to an applicant's name, what's the first thing that comes to your mind? What does it signal to you?

Can you recall an instance where you found a great candidate who was not labeled as 'Gold', or a 'Gold Candidate' who was clearly not a good fit? What happened in that situation?

Ideal Future
Tell me about any ranking or filtering tools you might use within your primary ATS. How do you use them, and what do you wish they could do better? 

Imagine a system that tried to score or rank candidates for you. What should be ranked and scored for you to trust its judgment?

On the flip side, what would make you immediately skeptical or distrustful of such a candidate score or recommendation?

If you could have a perfect assistant to help you sort through a large pile of applications, what would you ask it to do or to show you first?
